statusHistory.note: WILD0 piece from the verified Amsterdam war-room slate (BACKLOG.md/content/post-plan.md): the Binnenhaven at Marineterrein became Amsterdam Centrum's first officially designated open-water swim spot, announced by Waternet/Waterschap AGV on 2025-02-20 with the province of Noord-Holland approving the location, taking effect 'from April' 2025 at the start of the swim season — this checks out against multiple independent sources (Waternet, AGV, IamExpat, NL Times) and is stated plainly in the body rather than oversold. No lifeguard, no changing rooms/showers found in any source — swimming is explicitly 'at your own risk,' and the floating dock/vlonder closes for 72 hours after heavy rain when sewage overflow risk is high. Could NOT verify an exact opening address/entrance point beyond 'the Marineterrein site, reachable from Kattenburgerstraat' — geocode below is an approximate placement of the inner harbor (Binnenhaven), not a pinned entrance, and needs refinement. heroImage left null: searched Wikimedia Commons for a rights-clear photo of Marineterrein/Binnenhaven and found nothing usably licensed and specific to the swim spot itself (most Marineterrein-tagged Commons files are of unrelated naval-base buildings or the Scheepvaartmuseum next door). Illustration brief for near-illustrator: an inner-harbor dock scene, people swimming off a low composite boardwalk/pontoon between old naval-base brick facades, overcast Amsterdam light, no lifeguard tower, small digital info-screen showing water quality — should read as a real urban swim spot, not a beach resort. categories set to wellness-fitness (matches wild0's registered beat and the practitioner/access-focused lens); travel was considered but wellness-fitness fits an outdoor-swim-access piece better per categories.ts guidance. Status kept as draft pending geocode refinement and hero image resolution.
